transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came because… things with my in-laws aren’t just family disagreements. They’ve been using the church altar, and the parish committee, to push me out. Like they want everyone to forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you really believe your in-laws are using the church altar and parish committee against you?
Yes… I do. It’s not just arguments. I know they’ve been using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Have you noticed anyone else, besides your in-laws, behaving strangely towards you?
Mostly it’s them… my in-laws. I don’t know about everyone else. But at church, with the altar and the committee, it feels like they’ve gotten people to look past me, like I don’t matter anymore.
Do you think your in-laws' actions are targeted specifically at you?
Yes. I mean… that’s how it feels. It’s aimed at me—using the church and the committee to push me aside, like what I’ve done for the family doesn’t count.
Do you think there's any way to stop your in-laws from doing this to you, or do you think they'll keep trying no matter what?

I don’t know if it can really be stopped. I came in because I knew it wasn’t just family arguing… they were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make people forget what I’ve done for this family. So yes, I think they’ll keep trying.
Do you think your in-laws are plotting against you?
Yes… I think they are. Not in some obvious way, but using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
How long have you thought your in-laws were plotting against you?
About two months, I think… since that fight over the Día de los Muertos altar. That’s when all of this really started.
Do you think that events or conversations unrelated to you are somehow connected to you or planned with you in mind?

Yes… sometimes. Like the altar, and things with the parish committee… it didn’t feel separate from me. It felt like they were doing it with me in mind, to push me out and make people forget what I’ve done.
Do you think it's possible that your in-laws are not actually plotting against you?

I mean… I guess anything is possible. But it doesn’t feel that way to me. I came in because I knew they weren’t just arguing with me — it was the altar, the parish committee… it felt like they were trying to push me out and make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you think that things you see or hear on TV, or read in the newspaper, are referring to you?

Not really TV or the newspaper… it’s more what’s happening around me. The altar, the parish committee. I felt like my in-laws were using those things to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for the family.
Do you think that people are talking about you when you're not around?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I came in because it felt like my in-laws weren’t just arguing with me. They were using things like the altar and the parish committee to push me out… make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you think that your in-laws' actions are the only things that are referring to you, or do you think other unrelated things are also about you?
Mostly it’s them. I don’t think every little thing is about me… but the altar, the parish committee — that didn’t feel unrelated. It felt like they were using those things to push me out.
How long have you been thinking that your in-laws are using the church altar and parish committee against you?
About two months, I guess… since that fight over the Día de los Muertos altar. That’s when it all started feeling like this.
Do you think that things you see or hear in your daily life, outside of what your in-laws are doing, are somehow related to you or sent to you?

Not really… not outside that. It’s mostly what they’re doing with the altar and the parish committee. That’s what felt aimed at me — like they were trying to push me out and make people forget what I’ve done for the family.
Do you think that events or conversations with your friends or acquaintances, not including your in-laws, are somehow related to you or planned with you in mind?

No… not friends or people like that. It’s really my in-laws. They weren’t just arguing with me — they were using the altar and that parish committee to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for the family.
Do you think that things you see or hear in public, like on the radio or from strangers, are meant to convey a message to you?
No… not the radio or strangers. It’s not like that. It’s my in-laws… the altar, the parish committee. That’s where the message was, if you want to call it that. They were trying to push me out.
Do you think that things happening in your community, outside of your family and the church, are related to you or are about you?

No… not the community, really. I don’t think strangers or other things are about me. It was my in-laws, with the altar and that parish committee… trying to push me out and make people forget what I’ve done for the family.
Do you think that things that happen to you or around you, outside of what your in-laws are doing, have a special meaning or message for you?
No… outside of them, I don’t really think so. It’s mostly what I’ve said — my in-laws using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you think that your in-laws' actions against you are part of a larger plot involving other people or organizations?

I don’t know if I’d call it a larger plot. But it wasn’t just a simple argument. My in-laws were using the altar and the parish committee… to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you think that your in-laws are the only ones who are plotting against you or do you believe there are others involved as well?

It’s mostly my in-laws… but they had people around them, you know, the altar, the parish committee. So no, I don’t think it was just them alone. They were using all that to push me out… make everyone forget what I’ve done for the family.
